title: Limit previous-result check to the job a retry or follow-up continues
summary: The previous-result check in reading.rs currently runs over every job id cited in the request text. It should run only for the retried job (previous_job) and for jobs a request explicitly says it follows up. Jobs cited as evidence, such as the introspections in error-review root-cause requests, are shown to the reader as before and are not checked. The audience is the drain operator, who needs the drain to stop refusing those readings.

defaults_applied.how: New tests are added, and tests, clippy and fmt must pass.
The tests exercise accepted and refused readings rather than checking that code exists.
The check is scoped to the job being continued, not special-cased for root-cause requests.
One focused change in one source file plus the changelog.
The criteria check that the drain-stopping reading is accepted.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Follow-up detection is a small, documented phrase match on the request text, such as 'follows up job <id>' or 'follow-up of <id>'. It names the continued job. Other cited ids are evidence.
The retried job (the `attempt` argument of read_for, from previous_job) is always checked and its recorded result is given to the reader as now.
A followed-up job is carried to the reader with its recorded result, as the existing referenced_jobs carrying does. Evidence jobs are still carried but are not passed to check_prior_result_and_scope.
The scope check (deliverables and out_of_scope) keeps applying only when there is at least one continued job.
Only reading.rs and CHANGELOG.md change. No prompt files change, because the reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in reading.rs reads a root-cause request that cites two past jobs' introspections as evidence, with no previous_job and no follow-up wording. The reading does not restate those jobs' results and is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.

A new test shows that a retry whose reading omits the previous attempt's job id and result is still refused with 'the previous result'. A second test shows that the same retry with a reading that names the previous job is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.

A test shows that a request saying it follows up a named job is checked for that job only. A reading that omits the followed-up job is refused. A different job cited in the same request as evidence is not required to be named.

read_for passes check_prior_result_and_scope only the retried job and the explicitly followed-up jobs. Evidence-only referenced jobs are still given to the reader in the brief. The doc comments describe this distinction.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass, including the existing prior-result tests.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that the previous-result check applies only to the continued job and no longer refuses evidence citations.

out_of_scope: Changing the reader prompt files or the token budgets
Changing how the error review writes its requests
Changing the scope check (deliverables and out_of_scope) rules for genuine retries
Changing the MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS limit or the redaction of carried jobs
departures: Urgent, but the change is small and local. The reference is kept, with slightly higher acceptance because the request names files and tests.
urgent_reason: It cuts rejected attempts and stopped drains: the check refused a root-cause reading twice on 2026-10-27 and halted the drain.
hard_reason: This changes the gate that judges readings for other jobs, and a mistake would stop the drain again.
